# 1 Maccabees Chapter 3 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 3 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/1MA_003_page_001.jpg

---

1. And Judas his son, who was called Maccabeus, rose up in his place.
2. And all his brothers helped him, and all who had joined his father, and they fought the battle of Israel with gladness.
3. And he spread the glory of his people; and he put on a breastplate like a giant and girded himself with his weapons of war; and he set battles in order and protected the army with his sword.
4. And he was like a lion in his deeds, and like a lion's cub roaring for prey.
5. And he pursued the wicked and sought them out, and he burned with fire those who troubled his people.
6. And the wicked drew back for fear of him, and all the workers of lawlessness were troubled; and salvation was prospered in his hand.
7. And he embittered many kings, and made Jacob glad with his deeds; and his memorial is blessed forever.
8. And he went through the cities of Judah and destroyed the ungodly out of them, and turned away wrath from Israel.
9. And he was renowned to the ends of the earth, and he gathered those who were being lost.
10. And Apollonius gathered the nations together, and from Samaria a great and mighty force to make war against Israel.
11. And Judas heard and went out to meet him, and he struck him and killed him; and many fell slain, and the rest fled.
12. And he took their spoils, and Judas took the sword of Apollonius, and with it he fought all his days.
13. And Seron, the commander of the army of Syria, heard that Judas had gathered an assembly of faithful men and a congregation with him.
14. And he said, "I will make a name for myself and win glory in the kingdom; and I will make war against Judas and those with him, who have disregarded the command of the king."
15. And a powerful force of the ungodly went up with him to help him, to take vengeance on the sons of Israel.
16. And he approached as far as the ascent of Beth-horon, and Judas went out to meet him with a small company.
17. But when they saw the army coming to meet them, they said to Judas, "How shall we be able, few as we are, to fight against so great and strong a multitude? And we are faint, for we have eaten nothing today."
18. And Judas said, "It is easy for many to be shut up in the hands of a few; and there is no difference before Heaven whether to save by many or by few.
19. For victory in battle does not come from the multitude of the army, but strength is from Heaven.
20. They come against us in fullness of insolence and lawlessness to destroy us and our wives and our children, to plunder us.
21. But we fight for our lives and our laws.
22. And he himself will crush them before our face; but do you not be afraid of them."
23. And when he had finished speaking he fell upon them suddenly, and Seron and his army were struck before him.
24. And he pursued him in the descent of Beth-horon to the plain, and about eight hundred men of them fell, and the rest fled to the land of the Philistines.
25. And the fear of Judas and his brothers fell upon all the nations round about, and the fame of them reached the king, and all the nations talked about the battles of Judas.
26. And when King Antiochus heard these words, he was angry in his soul; and he sent and gathered all the forces of his kingdom, an exceedingly strong army.
27. And he opened his treasury and gave wages to his forces for a year, and commanded them to be ready for every need.
28. And he saw that the money in the treasury was exhausted, and the tribute of the country was little, because of the contention and the plague which he had made in the land by abolishing the customs which had been from the earliest days.
29. And he feared that he would not have enough as before for the expenses and gifts which he had given with a liberal hand previously, since he was above the kings who were before him.
30. And he was greatly troubled in his soul, and purposed to go to Persia, and to take the tribute of the countries and gather much silver.
31. And he left Lysias, a distinguished man of royal descent, to have oversight of the king's affairs from the river Euphrates to the borders of Egypt,
32. and to raise up his son Antiochus until he returned.
33. And he delivered to him half of the forces and the elephants, and gave him commands concerning all that he wanted, and concerning the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem:
34. that he should send an army against them to crush and root out the strength of Israel and the remnant of Jerusalem, and to take away their memorial from that place,
35. and to settle in their borders foreigners for all their land, and distribute their land by lot.
36. And the king took the remaining half of the forces and set out from Antioch, his royal city, in the one hundred and forty-seventh year; and he crossed the river Euphrates and went through the upper provinces.
37. And Lysias chose Ptolemy son of Dorymenes, and Nicanor, and Gorgias, mighty men of the Friends of the king,
38. and sent with them forty thousand foot soldiers and seven thousand horsemen to go into the land of Judah and destroy it according to the word of the king.
39. And they went out with all their force, and came and encamped near Emmaus in the plain country.
40. And the merchants of the country heard the report of them, and took silver and gold in very great quantities, and fetters, and came to the camp to take the sons of Israel for slaves; and the forces of Syria and the land of the strangers were added to them.
41. And Judas and his brothers saw that evils were multiplied and that forces were encamped in their borders, and they knew of the king's commands which he had commanded to do to the people for destruction and complete annihilation.
42. And they said, each to his neighbor, "Let us raise up the ruin of our people, and let us fight for our people and the sanctuary."
43. And the congregation was gathered together to be ready for battle, and to pray and ask for mercy and compassion.
44. And Jerusalem was uninhabited like a wilderness; there was none of her offspring who went in or went out; and the sanctuary was trodden down, and the sons of strangers were in the citadel; it was a lodging for the nations; and Jacob had lost his joy, and the pipe and the harp had ceased.
45. And they were gathered and came to Mizpah over against Jerusalem, for a place of prayer for Israel had formerly been in Mizpah.
46. And they fasted that day and put on sackcloth and put ashes on their heads, and tore their garments.
47. And they spread out the Torah scrolls which the nations had searched for to paint likenesses of their idols;
48. and they brought the priestly garments and the firstfruits and the tithes, and they raised up the Nazirites who had completed their days.
49. And they cried aloud toward Heaven, saying, "What shall we do with these men, and where shall we lead them?
50. And your sanctuary is trodden down and made profane, and your priests are in mourning and humbled.
51. And behold, the nations are gathered against us to destroy us; you know what they intend to do against us.
52. How shall we be able to stand before them, if you do not help us?"
53. And they sounded the trumpets and cried aloud.
54. And after this Judas appointed leaders of the people, commanders of thousands, commanders of hundreds, commanders of fifties, and commanders of tens.
55. And to those who were building houses, or were betrothed, or were planting a vineyard, or were afraid, he said to each to return to his house according to the Torah.
56. And they moved the camp and encamped south of Emmaus.
57. And Judas said, "Gird yourselves and be men of valor, and be ready in the morning to fight with these nations who have assembled against us to destroy us and our sanctuary.
58. For it is better for us to die in battle than to see the evils of our nation and the sanctuary.
59. As the will of Heaven is, so shall he do."
60. And Gorgias took five thousand footmen and a thousand picked horsemen, and this company moved out by night
